why: drops @Override from codec, streamCodec and keeps the method: it then overrides nothing and never runs -- port it to the new signature, or delete it and say what vanilla now does instead
reviewed: 26.1 made RecipeSerializer a final record (codec, streamCodec), so nothing can implement it and there is nothing to override (CATALOG M64): ModRecipes registers new RecipeSerializer<>(MAP_CODEC, STREAM_CODEC) built from this class's same codecs, which getSerializer returns; codec()/streamCodec() stay as plain accessors for ConfigRecipeManager and SyncDragonCrystalRecipesPacket, which hold an instance.

why: drops @Override from save and keeps the method: it then overrides nothing and never runs -- port it to the new signature, or delete it and say what vanilla now does instead
reviewed: The SavedData shape of CATALOG V29, as EnderDragonEvent (re-judged at 965926d): 26.1.2 SavedData has no save(CompoundTag, Provider) to override; get() goes through the shared mv.SavedDatas.computeIfAbsent(level.getDataStorage(), WraithSummonSavedData::new, (tag, provider) -> load(tag), "the_last_sword_wraith_bindings"), whose CompoundTag codec calls this public save reflectively (it never reads its registries argument), so the method still runs on every save; when the 26.x file data/the_last_sword/<name>.dat is absent, SavedDatas loads the dimension's 1.21.x data/<name>.dat once and marks it dirty.
